info.desc: Jagged Little Pill is the third studio album (and the first to be released internationally) by Canadian singer Alanis Morissette. The album made a sharp turn in genre and style for Alanis from her previous dance pop sound. The album garnered great success, spending twelve non-consecutive weeks at number one on the U.S. Billboard 200 albums chart, and became one of three albums – along with Thriller by Michael Jackson and Falling into You by Céline Dion – to remain in the Top Ten for over a year. podcast.body: Released in 1995, this post-grunge album was the outcome of a creative partnership with producer Glen Ballard, following two previous unsuccessful pop albums. Katy Perry lauded it as "the most perfect female record ever made" and a significant inspiration. The album sold an estimated 33 million copies, placing it among the 12th best-selling albums of all time, alongside works like Michael Jackson's *Bad*, Led Zeppelin's *Led Zeppelin IV*, and The Beatles' *Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band*. Only Shania Twain and Whitney Houston have achieved higher individual album sales among women. "The best estimate we have for sales is 33 million copies."

podcast.body: This chart-dominating blockbuster album took the Album of the Year prize at the 1996 Grammys. Its win showcased the immediate impact of the newly installed nominating committees, which aimed to bring more current music into the major categories. "Alanis Morissette, whose chart dominating blockbuster Jagged Little Pill took the prize."

podcast.body: Upon its release, this album marked a significant shift in Alanis Morissette's public image, transforming her from a "pop star with the poofy hair" into an "angry young woman." The album features the song "You Oughta Know," which sparked widespread speculation about the identity of the ex-boyfriend it describes. "people were shocked at how this pop star with the poofy hair had graduated into this angry young woman."

"After she blew up with her jagged little pill album in 1995, if you saw her can't not tour, Taylor was the drummer."
